newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Oil industry wants exclusion from EU worktime law.
newsitem.headline: Oil industry wants exclusion from EU worktime law.

text.p: The oil and gas industry said on Thursday it would try to keep national worktime rules and that it would press for the sector's continued exclusion from any new European Union offshore working time legislation.

The Oil Industry International Exploration & Production Forum reacted to a statement by the European Commission this week that EU rules on working hours and rest times should also apply to workers they do not currently protect.

"We understand and share the Commission's concerns about the importance of the health and safety of workers, particularly if there is a demonstrable lack of adequate protection in some of the sectors currently excluded from the working time directive," it said in a statement.
However, in the offshore sector, existing national regulations and the arrangements between employees, the national authorities and employers take these concerns fully into account, it added.
"Moreover, the excellent health and safety record of the industry speaks for itself and additional legislation at EU level would not improve the situation," it said.
"This is why we are disappointed that the (Commission's document) does not recommend the continuing exclusion of the offshore oil and gas sector."

It said it would point out during the consulation process on the proposals the need to maintain efficiency if employment and the international competitiveness of Europe's offshore oil and gas industry is to be maintained.
The body said it represents 60 oil and gas member companies worldwide.
The EU's working time directive guarantees workers a maximum 48-hour week, night shifts of an average of eight hours, four weeks paid leave a year and at least one day off a week.
